text: An application performs 20 round trips per operation. It is fine on the LAN and unusable over a WAN with plenty of bandwidth. Why?
choices: 20 round trips at 35 ms each is 700 ms of pure latency, and no amount of bandwidth reduces it
explanation: This is the durable form of the LAN/WAN distinction. Count round trips first, then consider bandwidth — a chatty protocol is a latency problem wearing a bandwidth costume, and the fix is protocol change or caching, not a bigger circuit.
